about.label: About
about.title: What is Dropper
about.desc: “Just drop in a file, and the hassle is handled.” We call these little tools Dropper, and we build and release them as a series. The first one reads an event document, adds the date and venue to Google Calendar, and even writes the WhatsApp/SNS announcement for you. The second reads a single sheet with many dates on it — a year planner, for example — and puts them all into your calendar at once. They all work the same way — just drop — so anyone can use them, not only a particular group or sport. More tools will be added over time.
privacy.metaDesc: DROPPER's privacy policy. How your data is handled, how the app accesses Google user data, and what is sent when the AI feature is used.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: DROPPER runs entirely in your browser. We operate no server of our own, and we never collect, store, or transmit your data.
privacy.s2body: DROPPER runs only in your browser. Nothing it reads and no file you drop is ever sent to a server of ours — we do not operate one. All processing happens within your own Google account.
privacy.s3title: 3. How we handle Google user data
privacy.s3body: With your permission, DROPPER accesses Google services within the following scopes.
privacy.s3r1b: To add the dates read from your event document or schedule to your own calendar.
privacy.s3r2a:
Access to files this app creates
(drive.file)
privacy.s3r2b: To read the text from your event document or schedule (OCR) and save the document to your own Google Drive.
privacy.s3r3b: To remember which folder your files are saved in, so the same folder is reused across your devices (for example, phone and computer).
privacy.s3n1: All of this data is processed inside your own Google account. We never receive any of it.
privacy.s3n2: drive.file is limited to files this app itself creates. It cannot see the rest of your Google Drive.
privacy.s3n3: Temporary files created for text recognition (OCR) are deleted immediately after the text is read.
privacy.s4notice: When the AI feature is used, the text read from your event document or schedule — or the file itself (PDF or image) — is sent to Google's Gemini API. Whether to use this feature is entirely your choice.
privacy.s4n1: Using AI is opt-in. After you sign in, a dialog asks you to choose "Use AI" or "Do not use AI".
privacy.s4n2: Only if you choose "Use AI" is the text read from your event document or schedule — or the file itself (PDF or image) — sent to Google's Gemini API.
privacy.s4n3: The request uses an API key that you obtain yourself. The key is stored only on your own device (in your browser's localStorage) and is never sent to us.
privacy.s4n4: Data sent to the Gemini API is handled under Google's own policies.
privacy.s4n5: If you choose "Do not use AI", no text is sent anywhere outside your browser and your own Google account.
privacy.s5body: Dropper does not sell, share, or transfer your Google user data to us or to any third party. Dropper has no server and never receives this data in the first place.
privacy.s5n1: The only exception is when you choose "Use AI". Only then is the text read from the event document or schedule — or the file itself (PDF or image) — sent to Google's Gemini API using your own API key. This is a direct transmission between you and Google, based on your choice, and does not pass through us.
privacy.s5n2: Data sent to the Gemini API is handled in accordance with Google's Privacy Policy.
privacy.s5n3: Apart from the above, we never disclose Google user data to any advertiser, analytics provider, or other third party.
privacy.s6body: Dropper uses the following mechanisms to protect your data:
privacy.s7body: Because Dropper has no server, we do not retain any of your Google user data. Only the following information is stored on your device (in the browser's localStorage), and we cannot access it:
privacy.s8body: DROPPER is currently provided free of charge, and we do not collect or store any payment information. If paid features are introduced in the future, this policy will be revised and the change announced.
privacy.s9title: 9. Compliance with the Google API Services User Data Policy
privacy.s9body: DROPPER's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
guide.metaTitle: How to use Event Dropper | Event document to Google Calendar
guide.metaDesc: How to use Event Dropper: drop an event document (PDF or image) and register the event to Google Calendar and Google Drive automatically. With screenshots.
guide.title:
Event Dropper
User Guide
guide.subtitle: For first-time users
guide.lead: Just drop the event document. The event goes to your Calendar and the file goes to your Drive — in one step. You can also create a WhatsApp/SNS post from the same details.
guide.s1body1: Dropper is a web tool that reads an event document (PDF or image), creates the event in your Google Calendar, and saves the file to your Google Drive.
guide.s1body2: No installation — it runs in your browser. Reading and registration all happen inside your own Google account. Dropper has no server and never stores your data.
guide.s2body: All you need is a Google account.
guide.st1body: Click "Sign in with Google" and choose your account.
guide.shot2alt: The Sign in with Google button
guide.st1scopeLead: Google will ask for permissions. Dropper requests only these three:
guide.st1sc1: Calendar events — to create the tournament event
guide.st1sc2: Drive files created by Dropper — to save the event document
guide.st1sc3: App configuration data — to remember your settings
guide.shot3alt: Google consent screen listing the three permissions
guide.shot3cap: The consent screen — only three permissions
guide.st2body: Drag and drop the event document PDF or image onto the drop area. You can also click to choose a file.
guide.shot4alt: Dropping an event document PDF onto the drop area
guide.shot4cap: Drag & drop, or click to choose
guide.st3body: The tournament name, date, venue, events and more are read automatically and shown on a card. Always check the results here. Anything wrong can be fixed on the spot.
guide.shot5alt: The result card showing tournament name, date, venue and events
guide.st4body: Click "Register" and everything goes to your Calendar and Drive.
guide.s4r2b: A folder tree <Year> Tournaments / <Month> / Tournament name / in My Drive (e.g. 2026 Tournaments / 09 /), with the event document inside
guide.shot7alt: Google Drive folder structure: year, month, tournament name
guide.s5body: For better reading accuracy you can use AI (Google Gemini). It's entirely your choice. The basic reading works without it.
guide.s5sub1body: After signing in, a popup asks whether to use AI. Choose "Use AI" and the API key screen opens.
guide.shot8alt: Popup asking whether to use AI
guide.s5k2: Sign in with your Google account
guide.s5k4: Copy the key and paste it into Dropper
guide.s5kfoot: It's free and takes about 3 minutes.
guide.shot9alt: API key modal with setup steps and a button to open AI Studio
guide.s5note1: 🔒 Your key is stored only on your device (browser). It is never sent to the developer.
guide.s5note2: ⚠️ On the free tier, submitted content may be used to improve Google's services. Do not drop confidential documents.
guide.s5body2: Your choice is remembered, so the popup won't appear again. To change it, click "AI settings" in the banner at the top of the screen.
guide.s6a1: Free for now. Paid plans are planned for the future.
guide.s6a2: Table tennis and several other sports. Pick one from the sport selector at the top of the screen.
guide.s6a3: You can edit the card directly before registering. Some document layouts are harder to read; using AI often helps.
guide.s6q4: How do I delete a registered event?
guide.s6a4: Delete it from Google Calendar and Drive as you normally would. Dropper has no delete function.
guide.s6a5: No. Dropper has no server. Only if you enable AI, the event document text is sent to Gemini using your own API key. See the privacy policy for details.
guide.s7body: For questions or bug reports, contact movie.pingpong@gmail.com. This is a one-person project, so replies may take a while.
privacy.s6n1: All communication takes place over an encrypted connection (HTTPS).
privacy.s6n2: Because Dropper has no server, your data is never stored under our control and is not exposed to external breaches on our side.
privacy.s6n3: Your Gemini API key and settings are stored only on your device (in the browser's localStorage) and are never transmitted to us or anyone else.
privacy.s6n4: All access to Google services and the Gemini API takes place under the authentication and authorization of your own Google account.
privacy.s7store1: Whether you chose to use the AI feature
privacy.s7store2: Your Gemini API key (only if you chose to use AI)
privacy.s7delLead: You can delete this data at any time in the following ways:
privacy.s7del1: Temporary files created for text recognition (OCR) are deleted immediately after reading.
privacy.s7del2: Events created in your Google Calendar and event documents or schedules saved to your Google Drive are managed by you and can be deleted from Google at any time (Dropper has no delete function).
privacy.s7del3: The API key and settings stored on your device can be deleted at any time from your browser settings.
privacy.s7del4: You can revoke Dropper's access to your Google account at any time from your Google Account security settings.
privacy.s10body: Any changes to this policy will be posted on this page. If a change is significant, it will also be announced within the tool.
privacy.s11body: For questions about this policy, please contact movie.pingpong@gmail.com.
privacy.s11analyticsBody: Dropper uses the following tools to understand site usage for the purpose of improving the service. These handle statistical information about site browsing and are unrelated to the contents of your Google Calendar or Drive (Google user data).
privacy.s11a1: Google Analytics: collects statistics such as page views and referrers using cookies. The information collected is anonymized usage statistics and does not identify individuals. Data is handled in accordance with Google's Privacy Policy.
privacy.s11a2: Visitor counter (hits.sh): counts and displays the number of page views. It does not use cookies.
privacy.s11a3: If you do not wish to allow cookies, you can disable them in your browser settings or use the Google Analytics Opt-out Add-on.
privacy.s12body: For questions about this policy, please contact movie.pingpong@gmail.com.
gsched.metaTitle: User guide | Add a whole schedule to Google Calendar (Schedule Dropper)
gsched.metaDesc: How to use Schedule Dropper. Drop a year planner or a fixture list and add every entry on it to Google Calendar at once — explained step by step with screenshots.
gsched.title:
Schedule Dropper
User guide
gsched.subtitle: For first-time users
gsched.lead: Drop one schedule. Every entry on it is read at once, you check the list, and then they all go into Google Calendar together.
gsched.s1body1: It reads a single sheet packed with dates — a year planner, a fixture list, a season calendar — and adds those entries to your Google Calendar all at once. Instead of typing dozens of entries by hand, you drop the file once.
gsched.s1body2: The difference from Event Dropper, the first tool in the series, is how many entries come off one sheet: Event Dropper takes one entry from one flyer, while Schedule Dropper takes many at once. Note that Schedule Dropper does not write WhatsApp/SNS announcements — that is an Event Dropper feature.
gsched.s2r1b: The owner of the calendar you want the entries added to.
gsched.s2r3b: Free for now. Only AI mode needs your own Gemini API key, which also has a free tier.
gsched.st1body: Press "Sign in with Google" and choose your account. Calendar and Drive permissions are needed so that entries can be added and the file can be read.
gsched.shot1alt: The opening screen with the "Sign in with Google" button
gsched.shot1cap: Sign in with Google and allow Calendar and Drive access first.
gsched.st2body: Many schedules show dates without a year. If the schedule itself states the year, leave this box blank — it is picked up automatically. If the dates show no year at all, type the year here.
gsched.st2note: If the sheet does not state a year and you leave the box blank, entries can end up on the wrong year. When in doubt, fill it in.
gsched.shot2alt: The reading-mode switch, the year box and the drop area
gsched.shot2cap: Choose how to read it and set the year before you drop the file.
gsched.st3body: Drag the PDF or image onto the area on screen. "Choose a file" works just as well.
gsched.shot3alt: Picking a schedule PDF from the file dialog
gsched.shot3cap: Drag and drop, or pick the file with "Choose a file".
gsched.st4body: Every entry that was read appears in a list. Start, End, Time, Entry and Location can all be edited on the spot. Untick anything you do not want added.
gsched.shot4alt: A list of entries with a tick box on every row
gsched.shot4cap: The number of entries found is shown. Leave only the ones you want ticked.
gsched.st5body: Press "Add all to Google Calendar" and every row that is still ticked goes into your calendar.
gsched.shot5alt: The "Add all to Google Calendar" button below the list
gsched.shot5cap: The ticked rows go into your calendar together.
gsched.s4body: There are two ways to read a schedule. Which one suits you depends on the shape of the sheet, so switch if the result is not what you expected.
gsched.s4r1b: Table-style sheets with one entry per row.
gsched.s4r2b: Calendar grids and heavily designed schedules.
gsched.s4grid: ⚠️ A calendar grid — the month-by-month layout used by school year planners — cannot be read in normal mode. Once the page is turned into plain text, the link between a date and its entry is lost. Always use AI mode for that shape.
gsched.shot6alt: The "Read it more accurately with AI?" dialog
gsched.shot6cap: Whether to use AI is up to you, and you can change it at any time.
gsched.s4k2: Follow "Open Google AI Studio" and create a key (a few minutes, free, with a Google account).
gsched.s4k3: Copy the key and paste it into the box.
gsched.shot7alt: The Gemini API key settings dialog
gsched.shot7cap: The key stays on your device and is never sent to or stored on our servers.
gsched.s4note1: 🔒 The key is stored only in your own browser. We run no server, so we never receive it. The Gemini API has a free tier of roughly 1,500 requests a day.
gsched.s4note2: ⚠️ On the free tier, what you send may be used to improve Google services. Do not drop confidential documents.
gsched.s4body2: If entries are missing after a normal-mode read, press "Read again with AI" above the list to run the same file through AI (an API key is needed).
gsched.s5body: Reading is not perfect. Always look through the list before you add anything.
gsched.s5sub1body: A ⚠ appears on dates that fall outside the year you set. These are never corrected automatically, because some schedules genuinely list such dates. Look at the row and either fix the date or untick it. "Clear ⚠ only" unticks every flagged row in one go.
gsched.s5sub2: With a long list, start small
gsched.s5sub2body: When there are dozens of entries, add just a few first and see how they look in your calendar before adding the rest. "Clear all" lets you start from nothing and tick only what you need.
gsched.s5sub3body: Rows that were added successfully are unticked automatically, so pressing the button again will not put the same entry in twice.
gsched.s5sub4body: "Select all", "Clear all" and "Clear ⚠ only" above the list switch the tick boxes in bulk.
gsched.s6a1: No. Table-style sheets with one entry per row read well, but heavily designed material such as a poster can lose its structure in normal mode and may not be read at all. Use AI mode for calendar grids.
gsched.s6q2: What happens if I leave the year blank?
gsched.s6a2: If the schedule states the year, it is picked up automatically. If it does not, the year cannot be worked out reliably, so typing it in is safer.
gsched.s6a3: You can correct it directly in the list before adding. If there is a lot to fix, reading again with AI often helps.
gsched.s6q4: Will dropping the same schedule twice create duplicates?
gsched.s6a4: Rows that were added are unticked, so pressing the button again will not duplicate them. Reloading the page and adding everything from scratch will, though — check your calendar in that case.
gsched.s6a5: Not in Schedule Dropper. Announcements are a feature of Event Dropper.
gsched.s6a6: No. Dropper has no server. Only when you use AI mode is the schedule file sent to Gemini using your own API key. See the privacy policy for details.
gsched.s7body: To keep the tools cheap, we do not offer one-on-one support. If something is not working, please go through the steps on this page again. When entries are missing, trying AI mode often improves the result.
apikey.metaTitle: How to get a Gemini API key | No credit card, 3 minutes, free tier | Dropper
apikey.metaDesc: How to get the Gemini API key used by Dropper's AI mode, in three steps. No credit card required, and nothing to pay inside the free tier. Your key is stored only in your own browser and is never sent to our server.
apikey.title:
How to get a Gemini API key
No card · 3 minutes · Free
apikey.catchMain: No more copy-paste, over and over.
apikey.catchSub: A free API key — no credit card — turns Gemini into a tool built for your job.
apikey.lead: AI mode runs on your own API key. "API key" sounds technical, but all you do is press one button on Google's own page and copy the text it gives you.
apikey.whatBody1: It is a spare key that lets Gemini be called from your own Google account. Dropper borrows that key to ask the AI, on your behalf, to read the file you dropped.
apikey.whatBody2: The key stays yours. Dropper never holds it for you — it sits inside your browser only. You can regenerate it or throw it away on Google's side at any time.
apikey.canTitle: What an API key lets you do
apikey.canDesc: AI tends to stop at being a tool you ask questions. With an API key it becomes a tool you hand the whole job to — from reading the sheet to registering the entries.
apikey.can1title: Hundreds of entries from one sheet
apikey.can1body: Schedule Dropper read 157 events from a single school year planner and registered them straight into Google Calendar. The work of pasting into a chat and retyping each line disappears entirely.
apikey.can2title: In a screen built for your task
apikey.can2body: Name, date, venue and deadline come out field by field, so you can fix them on the spot before registering. That is what a purpose-built tool can do with the AI's brain, and the official chat cannot.
apikey.can3title: Put your idle free tier to work
apikey.can3body: Your Google account comes with a free tier most people never touch. An API key is what unlocks it. There is no pay-per-use metering, so using it does not generate a charge. The AI you only asked questions before now reads your documents and registers the entries for you.
apikey.moneyTitle: Why there is nothing to worry about on cost
apikey.moneyBody: Getting an API key in Google AI Studio does not involve entering any payment details.
apikey.money1: 💳 No credit card screen ever appears. You start using it while there is simply no way to bill you.
apikey.money2: 🆓 The free tier is roughly 1,500 requests a day. One file read is one request, so personal use rarely comes close.
apikey.money3: 🛑 Going over the limit stops the requests — it does not charge you. For the rest of that day you can use standard mode without AI, and the free tier resets the next day.
apikey.safeTitle: Where the key you type actually goes
apikey.safeDesc: Dropper has no server. Here is exactly where your key goes.
apikey.safeR1b: Only on your own device (your browser's localStorage). It is not synced to your other devices either.
apikey.safeR2b: There isn't one. We cannot receive your key, or anything that was read from your file.
apikey.safeR3b: To Google's Gemini API only, and only to ask — with your key — that your own file be read.
apikey.safeR4b: Clearing your browser data removes the key. Deleting the key in Google AI Studio disables it immediately.
apikey.safeNote: 🔒 The same points are written out on this page:
apikey.stepsTitle: Three steps to get your key
apikey.stepsDesc: If you have a Google account, you need nothing else.
apikey.st1body: Use the button below to open Google's own page (aistudio.google.com). This is Google's site, not ours.
apikey.st2title: Sign in with your Google account
apikey.st2body: Sign in with the Google account you normally use. You will not be asked for payment details here.
apikey.st3title: Press "Create API key" and copy it
apikey.st3body: A string starting with "AIza…" appears. Copy it, paste it into Dropper's API key field, and you're done.
apikey.stepsFoot: ※ Keep your key to yourself. If someone does see it, delete that key in AI Studio and create a new one — the old key stops working.
apikey.q1: Could I be charged without noticing?
apikey.a1: There is no credit card on file, so there is no way to bill you. Going past the free tier stops that day's requests rather than charging you.
apikey.q2: What if my key is stolen?
apikey.a2: The key sits on your device only and is never sent to our server. If you are still uneasy, delete the key in Google AI Studio — it stops working the moment you delete it, and you can create a new one.
apikey.q3: If I use up the free tier, does the tool stop working?
apikey.a3: No. Standard mode, which does not use AI, keeps working. AI mode gets its free tier back the next day.
apikey.q4: Can I use it on confidential documents?
apikey.a4: On the free tier, what you send may be used to improve Google's services. Please do not put confidential documents through AI mode (standard mode sends nothing outside).
apikey.q5: Is the tool unusable without an API key?
apikey.a5: No. Standard mode works from the start with no key at all. AI mode is an extra option for people who want the reading to be more accurate.
apikey.ctaTitle: Got your key? Put it to work
apikey.bandTitle: AI mode needs no card, and costs nothing
apikey.bandDesc: AI mode reads more accurately, and it is the only way to read grid-style calendar planners. All it needs is one API key, free from Google. No credit card registration involved.
apikey.bandBtn: See how to get an API key
apikey.fromGuide: How to get a key, how it is kept safe, and why there is nothing to worry about on cost are all explained on a page of their own.
